title: が (but)
meaning: "~, but ~" — joins two contrasting clauses; also a soft introduction ("~, and…").
simpleExplanation: が between two clauses means "but": 日本語は難しいですが、面白いです "Japanese is difficult, but it's interesting". It joins two sentences into one, and the first clause usually keeps its polite form (ですが／ますが). It is also used as a soft opener: すみませんが… "Excuse me, but...". This が is not the subject particle; it comes after a full clause, not after a noun.
whenUsed: Contrasting two facts, disappointing results (I went but didn't buy anything), and polite lead-ins before a request.

diagram.translation: Japanese is difficult, but it's interesting.

examples.ja: 日本語は難しいですが、面白いです。
examples.reading: にほんごは むずかしいですが、おもしろいです。
examples.en: Japanese is difficult, but it's interesting.

examples.ja: 昨日デパートへ行きましたが、何も買いませんでした。
examples.reading: きのう デパートへ いきましたが、なにも かいませんでした。
examples.en: I went to the department store yesterday, but I didn't buy anything.
examples.note: Past contrast: went but didn't buy.

examples.ja: すみませんが、ペンを貸してください。
examples.reading: すみませんが、ペンを かしてください。
examples.en: Excuse me, but could you lend me a pen?
examples.note: Soft opener: すみませんが.

examples.ja: この店は安いですが、あまりおいしくないです。
examples.reading: この みせは やすいですが、あまり おいしくないです。
examples.en: This shop is cheap, but not very good.

examples.ja: 田中さんは来ましたが、山田さんは来ませんでした。
examples.reading: たなかさんは きましたが、やまださんは きませんでした。
examples.en: Mr Tanaka came, but Ms Yamada didn't.
examples.note: Two topics with は, contrasted with が.

similarGrammar.difference: でも starts a new sentence; が joins two clauses in one.
After a noun, が is the subject particle; after a clause, it is "but".

commonMistakes.wrong: 日本語は難しいです。が、面白いです。
commonMistakes.right: 日本語は難しいですが、面白いです。
commonMistakes.why: が joins clauses inside one sentence; to start a new sentence use でも.

commonMistakes.wrong: 高いですが、買いません。(when there is no contrast)
commonMistakes.why: が means "but". If the second clause follows logically from the first, use から.

commonMistakes.wrong: 高いが、買います。(in a polite conversation)
commonMistakes.why: In polite speech, keep です／ます before が.

usageNotes: In polite speech both clauses are usually polite (〜ですが、〜です). This が is a conjunction, not the subject particle (#6). Sentence-initial equivalent: でも (#68). けど (#67) is the casual counterpart.
jlptTips: If the two clauses contrast (difficult / interesting, went / didn't buy), the connector is が or けど. If the second follows from the first, it is から／ので.
すみませんが and 失礼ですが are fixed polite openers; expect が after them.
